# How to use .sdkmanrc

`.sdkmanrc` is a configuration file for SDKMAN used to specify a specific project or version of SDK under a directory.You can use `.sdkmanrc`： by following steps

1. The initialization environment：executes the following commands in the project or directory, and a `.sdkmanrc` file will be created in the current directory where the current environment is recorded.You can manually modify the file to specify a specific version.

    ```bash
    sdk env init
    ```

2. Toggle environment：execution of the following command will switch to the version of the SDCK specified in the `.sdkmanrc` file in the current directory.

    ```bash
    sdk env
    ```

3. Clears the environment used by the current shell in：can execute the following commands if you want to clear the environment used by the current shell.

    ```bash
    sdk env clear
    ```

4. Installation environment：can execute the following commands if you want to configure your environment before using a new project or directory.

    ```bash
    sdk env install
    ```

Note that the `.sdkmanrc` file is for specific items or directories, different items or directories can have different `.sdkmanrc` files to specify a different version of SDK.
